articles.title: Miss Brasil que perdeu coroa ficará internada até o fim da gravidez | G1
articles.standfirst: Modelo capixaba de 19 anos precisará de repouso absoluto nos próximos dois meses. Familiar desmentiu boatos de que ela estaria em estado grave e confirmou que novo exame apontou que ela e o bebê passam bem.
articles.summary: Modelo capixaba de 19 anos precisará de repouso absoluto nos próximos dois meses. Familiar desmentiu boatos de que ela estaria em estado grave.
articles.body:
Lara Marina Soares Tosta perdeu o título de Miss Brasil Supranational 2026 — Foto: Redes sociais

A modelo capixaba Lara Marina Soares Tosta, de 19 anos, que teve o título de Miss Brasil Supranational 2026 destituído nesta semana , precisará passar o restante de sua gravidez internada . A informação foi confirmada ao g1 pelo tio da jovem, que afirmou que a ex-miss e o bebê passam bem .

Segundo o familiar, Lara teve um "pequeno contratempo" relacionado à gestação. O tio disse, ainda, que relatos de que a modelo estaria em estado grave são, na verdade, boatos.

"Quero frisar mais para vocês: tem saído algumas coisas ‘aí’ nas redes sociais de que ela tá mal. Isso é tudo mentira, não é verdade. A Lara tá muito bem, o bebê tá bem", afirmou.

Ainda de acordo com o tio, a decisão de manter a modelo internada partiu da equipe médica para garantir um cuidado mais rigoroso na reta final da gravidez. Lara deve permanecer na unidade hospitalar por pouco mais de dois meses, até o dia do parto. Não foram divulgados detalhes sobre o diagnóstico e o local da internação.

"A Lara vai precisar ficar em observação, tem que ficar em repouso e ela vai ter que ficar no hospital até o final da gestação", detalhou o tio. "Os dois meses e pouco para frente aí, a Lara vai ter que ficar lá no hospital sendo acompanhada pelos médicos, porque está requerendo um cuidado maior".

O familiar falou, ainda, sobre questões emocionais enfrentadas pela jovem nos últimos dias. "Acho que ela passou por momentos muito tensos esses dias e eu não sei se isso influenciou ou não no que tá acontecendo, mas ela está precisando desses cuidados", completou.

Ainda segundo o tio, uma ultrassonografia realizada neste sábado (29) confirmou que o bebê está saudável e que a modelo, agora, precisa apenas de "descanso e tranquilidade para que o bebê venha com saúde e venha em paz".

Natural do município de Afonso Cláudio , na Região Serrana do Espírito Santo, Lara Marina perdeu o posto de Miss Brasil Supranational na última quarta-feira (26). Logo após o anúncio da perda, ela revelou em suas redes sociais que estava grávida, afirmando que havia descoberto a gestação em agosto, após retornar da etapa mundial do concurso na Polônia.

No entanto, a organização do Concurso Nacional de Beleza (CNB) contestou a versão da capixaba. Neste sábado (29), a entidade divulgou documentos médicos que apontam que a modelo já havia realizado um exame de ultrassonografia no dia 22 de abril. Na época, o laudo apontava uma gestação de sete semanas, indicando que Lara já sabia que estava grávida quase três meses antes de embarcar para o concurso em julho.

A organização ressaltou que a destituição não ocorreu como punição pela gravidez em si, mas sim pelas quebras contratuais decorrentes da ocultação do fato e de outras regras de conduta, como a alteração sem autorização de trajes oficiais da produção e falhas de comunicação.

Procurado pelo g1 , o coordenador do Miss Espírito Santo, Charles Souza, esclareceu que a coordenação estadual não tinha conhecimento do exame de ultrassom de Lara realizado em abril. Ele informou que só soube da gravidez após o retorno da jovem da Polônia, quando a rede de apoio a orientou a realizar novos exames.

"Neste momento, nosso foco é zelar pela saúde física e emocional de Lara Marina, que, independentemente de qualquer decisão administrativa, ela sempre será uma vencedora para nós. Seguimos acompanhando e torcendo por sua recuperação, pelo seu bem-estar e pela saúde do bebê", declarou o coordenador.

Com a destituição de Lara, a coroa de Miss Brasil Supranational 2026 foi assumida pela vice-campeã do concurso, Camilly Ceccon, representante de Costa Verde e Mar.

articles.title: Irregularidades eleitorais em Sergipe: Justiça recebe 58 denúncias | G1
articles.standfirst: De acordo com os dados, Aracaju é o município com o maior número de denúncias, com 33 registros. Em seguida, aparece Tobias Barreto, com oito.
articles.summary: Com 58 registros de irregularidades eleitorais em Sergipe, Aracaju lidera as denúncias feitas à Justiça Eleitoral pelo aplicativo Pardal nestas eleições.
articles.body:
A Justiça Eleitoral recebeu 59 denúncias de irregularidades eleitorais em Sergipe, até as 16h deste sábado (29). Os dados são do Pardal, ferramenta da Justiça Eleitoral destinada ao recebimento de denúncias sobre infrações e irregularidades na propaganda eleitoral. A campanha das Eleições 2026 começou oficialmente no dia 16 de agosto.

Até agora, as denúncias relacionadas à disputa pelo governo do estado somam 16 registros, o maior número entre os cargos em disputa. Em seguida, aparecem os deputados estaduais, com 15 denúncias, e os deputados federais, com 10.

Entre os municípios, Aracaju concentra o maior número de denúncias, com 33 registros. Tobias Barreto aparece na sequência, com oito.

Ferramenta Pardal é o sistema da Justiça Eleitoral para denúncias de propaganda eleitoral irregular — Foto: Reprodução/RBS TV/Arquivo

Por meio do Pardal, eleitores podem encaminhar denúncias à Justiça Eleitoral. O objetivo é facilitar a participação da sociedade na fiscalização do cumprimento das regras eleitorais e tornar mais ágil o encaminhamento de informações sobre possíveis irregularidades.

O Pardal está disponível gratuitamente para smartphones e tablets. Para acessar o aplicativo, a pessoa usuária deverá se identificar por meio do e-Título ou da plataforma Gov.br. A Justiça Eleitoral garante que o denunciante permanecerá protegido por sigilo, independentemente da forma de autenticação utilizada.

Ao registrar uma denúncia, a pessoa usuária deverá descrever a suposta irregularidade. Em seguida, um agente automatizado fará uma classificação preliminar da ocorrência em duas categorias: propaganda eleitoral irregular na internet e demais modalidades de irregularidades na propaganda eleitoral.

articles.title: How a chance meeting at Dollywood led to the deepest friendships of their lives
articles.summary: SEVIERVILLE, Tenn. - The reunion began at dusk here, outside the small courthouse square that had become an impromptu shrine to hometown legend Dolly Parton....
articles.body:
How a chance meeting at Dollywood led to the deepest friendships of their lives

SEVIERVILLE, Tenn. - The reunion began at dusk here, outside the small courthouse square that had become an impromptu shrine to hometown legend Dolly Parton.

Robbie Thompson had flown in from Orlando. Garner Byram Jr. had raced south from Waynesboro, Virginia. Libby Rollf had rushed in from Kansas City, Kansas. Others made their way from Dayton, Ohio; Asheville, North Carolina; and elsewhere in Tennessee and Florida.

"We gravitated here because we need each other now," said Aaron Hamby, 30, of South Carolina, about what drew them once again to East Tennessee, where most of them had met years earlier.

Those who had arrived this Wednesday evening carried bouquets of roses, wore T-shirts from past Dolly concerts and hugged the way old friends do. They were young and not-so-young, straight and gay and transgender, married and unmarried. They work in health care and education, in government and in the airline industry. They have varying political views and economic means.

But for all their differences, the small group had forged a bond over time that runs far deeper than the music. Their shared love of Parton had given them something precious: a community some had never expected to find.

"We've become like a family. A Dolly family," said Thompson, 44. "We like this family more than some of us like our own families."

On a week when much of the nation remembered Parton as someone who embraced people of all stripes and transcended so much that divides the country, here was a living manifestation of her power to unite. A group of far-flung souls who had first met in line on a long-ago day at Dollywood and forged a bond deepened by time.

Many of them have traveled the nation and the world together to see Parton, from London to Red Rocks in Colorado. Their reunions have unfolded in South Dakota, Oklahoma, Kansas, Iowa and all over the East Coast. They have come to nearly every opening day at the Dollywood theme park, spent too much money on travel, burned too much vacation time - and had a blast doing it.

"We paid for her last tour bus, honey," Byram, 42, joked.

Their faithfulness to Dolly has sometimes strained relationships in their daily lives. "My ex told me we broke up because Dolly came between us," he said, with little remorse.

Fifteen years on, even as their numbers have grown and changed, this small group has remained loyal to their patron saint - and to one another.

Now, they had gathered again to celebrate her luminous life, to grieve her passing and to give thanks for bringing them together.

"This is where I feel most at home," Thompson said. "Here with my people."

There was Dolly's celestial voice, of course. And her soul-filled mountain music. But for many of the friends, there was something else that drew them to her decades ago.

"Acceptance," Thompson said Thursday on the porch of a cabin the group had rented together near Great Smoky Mountains National Park.

Growing up gay and feeling out of place in small-town Virginia, he was struck by Parton's insistence that it was okay to be who you are, no matter what.

"That message resonated with me from a very early age," he said.

It was much the same for Byram, who first saw Dolly with his parents in the early 1990s.

"She was her own unique person, so you could be, too," he said. "You could tell that she didn't judge anybody."

That message made its way to Rollf, 50, who as a girl in Kansas remembers listening to Parton in her father's blue Chevy truck and becoming obsessed with her music.

"I was a very overweight child," she said. "And she was just so accepting. She was just a ray of sunshine."

As childhood gave way to adulthood, they and others in the group made numerous pilgrimages to Dollywood, even when few others in their lives understood why they were so drawn to her presence.

"I did it for so many years alone," Brittany Mixon, 51, of Pensacola, Florida, who also was there as a 10-year-old the day the park opened in 1986.

About 15 years ago, the group began to discover one another after several of them met by chance outside an event where Dolly was greeting fans at the park.

They began traveling together to shows around the country and returning to Pigeon Forge almost anytime Parton was scheduled to appear at Dollywood. They embraced Rollf's mother, who often traveled with the group, dubbing her the "Dolly Mama."

Over time, they found, their friendships only deepened.

When Byram's mother died, Thompson and Rollf traveled unannounced to be with him in Virginia.

"They just show up for you," he said. "It would be just absolutely miserable without them. … My life is totally different because of them."

When Rollf's mother died unexpectedly years later, numerous members of the group showed up at her door in Kansas the next day.

They call one another on birthdays and even email Shoney's gift cards. They send each other Christmas presents. They commiserate over breakups and job changes. They maintain an endless text chain, and always check on one another by noon each day.

"If you are having a bad day, you can call any one of them," said Carrie Reinig, 52, who lives in Ohio. "We celebrate each other's successes and support each other when things are crappy. … They are legit family."

Could those deep ties weaken now that Parton, their north star, has died? Could the thread that held them together all these years fray?

"I don't feel that part will change," Reinig said. "If anything, we will probably need each other more."

Thursday evening in the mountainside cabin, more than a dozen Dolly-loving friends gathered to laugh and shed tears, share old photos and reminisce about their many encounters with the singer.

Some cars in the driveway had Dolly-themed license tags and bumper stickers with phrases such as "Dolly vibes only." At least two attendees had Dolly's signature tattooed on their arms.

Inside, a Dolly-branded peach cobbler baked in the oven. The living room television was playing a Dolly marathon - the movie "Steel Magnolias," a documentary of her career, and a replay of her 50th anniversary performance at the Grand Ole Opry. Virtually everyone in the room had attended that show.

"How are you doing?" one person asked Kimberly Baker-Boyle, 55, who moved to East Tennessee from Maryland with her husband and daughters more than a decade ago, mostly to be closer to the Dollyverse.

"You know, it's like losing your mother," she said, sighing.

"This time is different. … Usually we are riding high," said Jonathan Brashier, 52, of Greenville, South Carolina, who has been coming here since the 1980s.

That day, a sadness lingered in the room, even though the friends were comforted by one another's presence.

"I always imagined we'd be together on a night like this," Brashier said.

They talked about the plans they had to see Dolly, the music and memories that now will not happen.

"How many of us had tickets to Las Vegas?" one asked of a planned residency there that Parton had previously postponed and then canceled altogether.

They talked about the countless times they met Parton at Dollywood, about the scores of shows they attended - for some, more than two dozen on one tour alone. They laughed at the outrageous sums some spent on front-row concert tickets or meet-and-greets or traveling to distant shows.

They vowed to stay close, whatever lies ahead.

"The biggest gift [Dolly] gave us is the friendship and relationships with each other," said Hamby. "Now that the inevitable has happened, that's what is going to carry on … these bonds we share."

At the end of the night, there were hugs and I-love-yous, and posing for pictures together in their many colors of Dolly shirts.

Outside, in the warm August night, the only sound came from the hum of cicadas. A full moon hung over the Smoky Mountains, its light shimmering off the Little Pigeon River.

Early Friday, in the light of a clear blue morning, the group of friends drove down the mountainside and headed north toward Sevierville.

In Pigeon Forge, they passed the glittering entrance to Dollywood, where they planned to return later in the day to visit the place they had first met and carved out so many happy memories. It would be healing, they thought, to commune with fellow mourners pouring into town from Georgia, Ohio, Texas, Alabama, New York and even Canada.

On they drove, past so many flags at half-staff. Past the pancake houses and souvenir shops, past the dinner theaters and mini-golf courses. Past signs that proclaimed "We will always love you, Dolly" outside Andy's Frozen Custard and the Suds car wash and the Sonic drive-in.

Outside the county courthouse, they gathered once again in front of the statue of Dolly, where dozens of pink buckets had been set up to hold the endless flowers and notes from fans.

They carried bouquets of yellow roses and colorful cardboard butterflies. Thompson wore a shirt that read, "In Dolly We Trust." Byram slid on his sunglasses to shield his tears.

"I woke up heavier today than yesterday," Brashier said to no one in particular.

They walked together to the statue, which they had visited so many times on happier days, and stood with their arms wrapped around one another, heads on shoulders, in silence.

After a few minutes, Byram asked a stranger nearby if he could snap a photo of the group of friends in front of Dolly.

"You want the whole family in there?" the man asked.

articles.title: Flood fears in Bihar as several rivers cross danger marks amid Nepal rains
articles.summary: PATNA: Flood fears intensified in Bihar on Saturday as persistent rains in Nepal and the state caused water levels in several rivers to rise above dan.
articles.body: PATNA: Flood fears intensified in Bihar on Saturday as persistent rains in Nepal and the state caused water levels in several rivers to rise above danger marks.The rivers were already swollen following flash floods in the neighbouring Himalayan nation earlier this week.According to the Water Resources Department, the Gandak river has crossed the danger mark in Gopalganj, while the barrage at Valmikinagar released around 99,800 cusecs of water at 8 pm on Saturday.Wednesday’s flash flood in Nepal, triggered by an ice-rock landslide, has prompted the administrations in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar to intensify monitoring of river systems downstream of the Himalayan rivers."The water level of several rivers, including the Gandak, Kosi, Burhi Gandak and the Ganga, has been rising. Incessant rainfall in the catchment areas of Nepal has led to rivers touching or flowing above the danger level at several places," a senior official of the Water Resources Department told news agency PTI on Saturday.The Kosi and Burhi Gandak rivers have reached the danger level in Khagaria, Katihar and Kursela, while the Ganga is flowing above the danger mark at Hathidah and Gandhighat in Patna, as well as Kahlgaon in Bhagalpur, according to a Water Resources Department bulletin.People residing in low-lying areas have been moved to safety, said a senior official, adding that all departments concerned have been put on alert."District magistrates have been directed to monitor the situation personally. articles.title: Quote of the day by Queen Elizabeth: "But let us not take ourselves too seriously. None of us has a monopoly of…" - a timeless advice on respecting opinions different from your own
articles.summary: UK News: Queen Elizabeth’s words offer a quiet reminder that wisdom never really belongs to just one person, and that genuine humility is essential when dealin.
articles.body: Queen Elizabeth’s words offer a quiet reminder that wisdom never really belongs to just one person, and that genuine humility is essential when dealing honestly with other people. "But let us not take ourselves too seriously," she said. "None of us has a monopoly of wisdom, and we must always be ready to listen and respect other points of view." She said this during her Christmas broadcast in 1991, one of the annual addresses she delivered to the United Kingdom and the Commonwealth throughout her seventy-year reign, and it has remained one of her most quoted lines ever since. Her words challenge a fairly common assumption, that being experienced, successful, or simply in a position of authority somehow means having all the answers. The quote encourages people instead to remain genuinely open to different opinions, to listen properly before judging, and to recognise that another person's perspective might well offer something we have quietly missed ourselves.Quote of the day by Queen Elizabeth"But let us not take ourselves too seriously. None of us has a monopoly of wisdom, and we must always be ready to listen and respect other points of view"Understand the meaning behind Queen Elizabeth's quoteThe quote suggests that nobody, however experienced or well informed, has a complete understanding of absolutely everything. We all carry different experiences, different knowledge, and genuinely different ways of looking at the world around us. Even at moments when we feel entirely confident that we are right about something, someone else may well have information or lived experience that quietly changes how we actually see the whole situation. That is precisely why Queen Elizabeth's message places such real importance on listening properly, and on respecting a point of view even when it differs sharply from our own.Why nobody genuinely has a monopoly on wisdomThe phrase "monopoly of wisdom" describes the belief that only one person, or one particular group, actually possesses the correct knowledge or understanding on a given subject. That kind of attitude, however confidently held, tends to prevent genuinely meaningful conversation from ever really happening. A person can be highly educated or vastly experienced and still, quite genuinely, have something left to learn. Equally, someone with considerably less formal experience may well offer an insight that everyone else in the room had simply overlooked. Real wisdom, in that sense, tends to turn up in fairly unexpected places, often from people nobody thought to ask in the first place.Why listening is genuinely a form of strengthListening is sometimes quietly mistaken for passivity, as though someone who listens carefully must simply be going along with whatever they hear. In reality, being genuinely willing to listen requires considerable confidence in its own right. It means honestly accepting that your own understanding of a situation may not be complete after all. A good listener does not necessarily agree with everything they hear either. They simply give the other person enough real attention to properly understand their reasoning before deciding, calmly, how to actually respond. That small shift alone can make a genuine disagreement considerably more productive than it would otherwise have been.Respect does not require agreementOne of the most genuinely useful lessons hiding inside this quote is the real distinction between respecting someone's viewpoint and actually agreeing with it. People can hold completely different opinions on something while still treating each other with real courtesy throughout. Respect, understood properly, means recognising another person's genuine right to hold a perspective, even at moments when you honestly believe that perspective to be mistaken. That distinction becomes considerably more important precisely during a genuine disagreement, when it would be far easier to let respect quietly slip away entirely.Why taking ourselves too seriously can genuinely be limitingQueen Elizabeth opens with the line, "let us not take ourselves too seriously." That does not mean genuinely important matters should be treated lightly, or turned into a joke. It can instead be understood as a gentle reminder not to become so attached to our own sense of importance, or our own certainty, that we quietly stop listening to anyone else around us. Real humility allows a person to admit honestly that they can be wrong, to actually change their mind when the evidence calls for it, and to genuinely learn from their own mistakes rather than defending them out of pride.How different perspectives can genuinely improve a decisionA single perspective, however well informed, can still overlook something genuinely important. When people carrying different experiences examine the very same problem together, they very often identify a risk, an opportunity, or a solution that one person working entirely alone would never have noticed. This is exactly why listening properly matters so much within families, workplaces, and wider communities alike. A genuine disagreement, handled well, can actually improve an idea rather than simply weaken it.Other memorable quotes by Queen Elizabeth"It has always been easy to hate and destroy. To build and to cherish is much more difficult.""Work is the rent you pay for the room you occupy on earth.""I know of no single formula for success, but over the years I have observed that some attributes of leadership are universal and are often about finding ways of encouraging people to combine their efforts, their talents, their insights, their enthusiasm and their inspiration, to work together.""Everyone is our neighbour, no matter what race, creed, or colour."How to practise Queen Elizabeth's messageListen before responding, genuinely giving other people the time they need to properly explain their own point of view.Accept honestly that you can be wrong, since real confidence has never actually required constant certainty.Ask genuine questions, trying to understand exactly why someone sees an issue so differently from you.Avoid dismissing an unfamiliar opinion too quickly, since a different perspective can still contain something genuinely valuable.Separate disagreement from disrespect, since you can challenge an idea firmly without ever attacking the person holding it.Stay genuinely curious, treating an ordinary conversation as a real opportunity to learn something new.Admit your own mistakes honestly, since changing your mind when presented with better information is a genuine strength, not a weakness.Avoid assuming you already have all the answers, since real experience has never actually made anyone infallible.Give other people proper credit, recognising a good idea even when it comes from someone who genuinely disagrees with you.Keep your own sense of humour intact, since not every disagreement genuinely needs to become a personal battle.Why Queen Elizabeth's quote remains relevantModern conversations can slip fairly easily into two opposing camps, people entirely convinced they are right, and people they are equally convinced are wrong. Queen Elizabeth's words offer a considerably quieter approach instead. Nobody genuinely has all the answers. Listening properly does not make you any less knowledgeable, and respecting another person's perspective does not actually require you to abandon your own beliefs in the process. The real strength lies in being genuinely confident enough to stay open to learning something new. Sometimes the wisest thing a person can actually do is simply pause for a moment, listen honestly to another point of view, and accept that there may still be something out there they genuinely do not yet know.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: US News: British far-right political commentator Milo Yiannopoulos has been deported back to the UK from the US after being detained by Immigration and Customs.
articles.body: British far-right political commentator Milo Yiannopoulos has been deported back to the UK from the US after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in Louisiana, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said.Yiannopoulos, 41, was arrested on Thursday at Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport after arriving in the US. He had entered the country legally in May 2019 but later overstayed his visa, according to DHS.An immigration judge issued a final order of removal on July 22 after Yiannopoulos failed to appear for an immigration hearing, AP News reported.A DHS spokesperson said Yiannopoulos was sent "back to his home country" on Friday, describing him as an "illegal alien from the United Kingdom"."He chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation's laws," the spokesperson said, according to the BBC.Who is Milo Yiannopoulos?Yiannopoulos, who grew up in Kent, England, rose to prominence as an editor at conservative US website Breitbart News. He later worked with rapper Ye, formerly known as Kanye West, and was also associated with former Republican congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene.A vocal supporter of Donald Trump during the 2016 presidential campaign, Yiannopoulos has backed the Trump administration's tougher immigration policies.He has previously called for mass deportations and urged ICE to deport people unable to prove they were legally in the US.Yiannopoulos later became critical of Trump while continuing to support parts of his political agenda.He has courted controversy over comments about immigrants, Islam, feminism, transgender people and other issues.In 2017, he resigned from Breitbart and was disinvited from the Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) after comments about sexual relationships between adults and minors resurfaced. He later apologised and said he had been discussing his own experiences as a child.His arrest was welcomed by far-right activist and Trump ally Laura Loomer, who has publicly feuded with Yiannopoulos. articles.title: Dolphins Are Learning a Clever Fishing Trick from Their Mothers
articles.summary: Some dolphins in Australia have figured out a hunting trick so unusual that scientists are only beginning to study it, and the way young calves are picking i...
articles.body:
Dolphins are known for being some of the most intelligent and adaptable animals in the world. Their intelligence is evident in their hunting methods, as they have the ability to use tools while searching for food. A group of dolphins in Australia have developed a particularly unusual way of hunting fish by using empty seashells to help them catch their prey. There's also evidence that young dolphins are learning the technique from their mothers by copying their behavior. So, how does this unusual method work, and what does it tell us about dolphins?

Although dolphins have previously been observed using tools, there is no other hunting strategy quite like the one seen in dolphins in Australia. A recent study has observed dolphins using a strategy known as shelling. Shelling consists of the dolphins chasing fish into an empty shell, effectively using the shell as a temporary trap. They then carry it up to the surface with the fish still in it. Once at the surface, they tilt the shell, tipping the fish out of the shell and straight into their mouth. Effectively, they use the empty shell as a container to catch and eat fish that might otherwise escape.

The study focused on Indo-Pacific dolphins in the Great Sandy Marine Park in 2025. Shelling had previously been observed in dolphins in Shark Bay in Western Australia. The two locations are thousands of miles apart, which suggests that the populations have learned how to use the technique independently. Dolphins using the shelling technique were also photographed in Queensland in 2013 and 2019. However, the technique had largely gone unnoticed due to the lack of research into dolphins in the area. The 2025 study is the first time the behavior has been officially studied outside of Shark Bay, and was seen in just a few individuals. This also suggests that it remains a specialized technique rather than widespread behavior.

Young dolphins can learn certain behaviors and techniques by watching other dolphins interacting and foraging. They also spend a lot of time watching their mothers forage. By doing this, they can learn which techniques work and which don't before attempting to replicate the behavior themselves. This is known as social learning. When the young dolphin learns specifically from their mother, it is known as vertical social learning.

Dolphin calves remain with their mother for a long time. This is often around six years, but they can sometimes stay with them for longer. Although they are weaned from their mother's milk by the time they are two or three years old, they spend the rest of the time learning the important behaviors that they need to survive. This long period of learning is particularly useful for dolphins. This is because they need to learn where to find food and how to catch it, as well as how to notice and steer clear of danger.

During the study, one dolphin calf appeared to copy its mother as she used a shell for catching prey. The calf picked up the shell within minutes of its mother dropping it. It was then spotted with a lizardfish dangling from the shell at the surface. This suggests that shelling could be a behavior that young dolphins learn from their mother.

Shelling is not the only example of dolphins using objects to help them catch their prey. Some Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins in Shark Bay have also been observed using marine sponges to protect their snout while searching on the seafloor for a meal. The dolphins break the sponge off from the seafloor and then hold it over their closed beak like a glove as they search in the seabed for food. The sponge protects their sensitive snout from rocks or stingrays.

A study found that "sponging", as it is named, is predominantly used by females. It also found that female calves with mothers that use the sponging method are also more likely to use sponging themselves. Therefore, it is believed that the knowledge of sponging is passed on through vertical social learning .

Sponging provides an interesting comparison to shelling and shows that dolphins learn more than one specialized hunting method from their mothers. Interestingly, this is now evidence of two different examples of tool use by dolphins in the same location. Both behaviors also show that dolphins can make use of objects that they find in their environment. They also show that, although some of the behaviors might not be instinctive, they can be picked up by dolphins who have watched others use them successfully.

articles.title: Frinton Normandy veteran who lied about age to enlist dies
articles.summary: A veterans' charity says Donald Turrell will be remembered with "enormous affection and gratitude".
articles.body:
A World War Two veteran who fought in the Normandy campaign after lying about his age has died aged 101, a charity has said.

Born in London in 1925, Donald Turrell was just 17 when he enlisted, having forged a letter from his parents to say he was 18.

His battalion crossed over to France in June 1944 in the days following D-Day and Turrell landed on Sword Beach before taking part in fierce fighting.

On Saturday, the Taxi Charity for Military Veterans said in a post on Facebook it was "deeply saddened" to share that Turrell, who recently lived in Frinton-on-Sea, Essex, had died on Friday, surrounded by his family.

Turrell joined the Cameronians (Scottish Rifles) and in the following months was stationed at Bury St Edmunds, Newquay, Newcastle and Fort William.

The charity's vice president, Dick Goodwin, said: "Don was incredibly special.

"He had a warmth and presence that lit up every room he entered, and he touched the lives of so many people.

"As a World War Two veteran, Don represented a generation whose courage and service we will never forget.

"It was a privilege for the taxi charity to know him, and he will be remembered with enormous affection and gratitude.

"My thoughts are with his family and all those who loved him at this very sad time."

In an interview last year, Turrell said: "I did lie about my age. I pushed it up a bit, gave all the right answers, and I was in. I was happy."

He explained he had always wanted to be a soldier and that like "all the young lads" he had wanted to play his part in defending his country.

The veteran described feeling "excited and apprehensive" during the crossing to the Normandy coast, and said his "introduction" to the war was seeing bodies from earlier fighting washing back up on the beach as he landed.

His war came to an end a few weeks later on July 10, when he was seriously injured during fighting near the town of Eterville. He was later medically discharged.

Turrell spoke movingly of the close friends he lost during the campaign, some of whom he buried in the field, and who are now buried in Commonwealth war cemeteries on the continent.

The war also claimed his older brother Leslie, who had been a telegraphist on HMS Penelope and died when she was sunk off the Italian coast near Naples in February 1944.

articles.title: Is the viral video really Kai Cenat being assaulted by police? Here’s the truth
articles.summary: US Streamers News: A video claiming to show streamer Kai Cenat being assaulted by a police officer has gone viral across social media, sparking outrage among viewers who.
articles.body: A video claiming to show streamer Kai Cenat being assaulted by a police officer has gone viral across social media, sparking outrage among viewers who believed the popular creator was involved. However, the footage has been misidentified. The man seen in the video is not Cenat, and the incident actually occurred during a traffic stop in Blytheville, Arkansas. The real confrontation involved a passenger and a state trooper, while Cenat had no connection to the incident.Viral Kai Cenat police assault video was misidentifiedThe footage circulating online does show a genuine confrontation between a police officer and a man, but claims identifying the person as Kai Cenat are false. According to the report, the incident occurred earlier this month in Blytheville, Arkansas, after a trooper stopped a vehicle that had allegedly been traveling at a dangerous speed.The situation reportedly escalated when a passenger resisted the officer's commands. The trooper then broke the vehicle's rear window and physically removed the passenger from the car. The man subsequently faced charges related to obstruction and resisting.While the use of force shown in the footage has prompted discussion online, the key issue surrounding the viral post is the identity of the person involved. It was not Kai Cenat.The confusion appears to have been fueled by the man's resemblance to Cenat. Once social media accounts attached the streamer's name to the clip, the claim quickly spread, with users sharing the footage alongside captions suggesting that Cenat had been confronted by police.Cenat is a hugely recognizable figure online, making the false identification particularly easy to spread. The streamer has also had previous encounters with law enforcement, including his 2023 arrest following the chaotic Union Square giveaway in New York, which may have made the new claim appear believable to some viewers.Why the false Kai Cenat claim spread so quicklyThe incident highlights how quickly misleading captions can transform real footage into a completely different story. A dramatic police confrontation already has the potential to attract attention, but attaching the name of a major streamer like Cenat can dramatically increase its reach.According to the report, the false claim gained momentum after users connected the footage to Cenat without checking its original source or comparing the identities of the people involved. The result was widespread outrage over an incident the streamer was never part of.The episode also demonstrates the risks of sharing viral clips without verifying their context. Even when the underlying footage is authentic, the description attached to it can be completely false.Ultimately, the police encounter shown in the video is real, but the claim that Kai Cenat was the person assaulted or arrested is not. The footage originated from a traffic stop in Arkansas and involved another individual.
